reconciliation: Four suites and three cross-cutting properties. There is no unit suite. What exists is the equivalence corpus, which proves AGREEMENT and not CORRECTNESS — a bug-for-bug port is green on a violation both engines share.
note: docs/PHASE1_BRIEF.md §7 lists seven suites. This file is the reconciliation with what is actually on disk, not a transcription of that table. Consumed by the CI workflows (job matrix), the dashboard (one row per entry; a missing result renders RED) and tests/manifest/manifest.test.ts (every claim here is checked). Timings measured on a 20-core machine, 18 Aug 2026; CI wall time will differ.

suites.title: Equivalence corpus
suites.proves: The ported TypeScript engine behaves identically to tools/legacy/v2_engine.js, action for action, comparing state plus RNG draws plus result after every action.
suites.doesNotProve: That the rules are CORRECT. This is an oracle for agreement: a bug-for-bug port is green on a violation both engines share, so identical games say the port matches legacy and nothing about whether legacy was right. It is also blind by construction to anything JSON destroys, because rig.ts normalise() round-trips BOTH engines through JSON before hashing — which is why the property suite carries viewstate-round-trip.

per-push.scale: 210 recorded games (200 per-push batch + 10 smoke), plus every non-corpus assertion

suites.title: Property / invariant suite
suites.proves: That ten stated invariants hold over generated legal play. The first instrument here that asks whether the rules are TRUE rather than whether two engines agree.
suites.doesNotProve: Coverage of the engine — it checks ten claims, and a rule nobody stated is a rule nobody is checking. Nothing about difficulty or balance. Nothing about multiplayer: single-player only, the three allocation actions are Phase 3. memory-on-kill is checked in the command phase only.

nightly.scale: 10,002 games, 1,032,791 states; exits non-zero if any invariant checked nothing

suites.title: Balance metric panel
suites.proves: That the engine still behaves the way the bands were measured on. FAIL means 'the rules changed under us'.
suites.doesNotProve: Difficulty, and it is not a win-rate gate — PHASE1_BRIEF §7 calls this 'win-rate regression with tolerance bands' and that is wrong; §4 forbids gating on a win rate. A green panel means 'no broad shift detected', NEVER 'the change was safe': it does not fail on brain branch:3 to 4, a demonstrated blind spot pinned in metrics-control.test.ts. The reference bot plays ~6 of 14 seats and wins ~0% on Normal where humans win essentially every game.

per-push.scale: one unseen arm per difficulty, 6,000 games

nightly.scale: one unseen arm per difficulty, 6,000 games — the same check, run unconditionally rather than only on a push that touched the engine

manual.scale: 24 arms + held-out, 150,000 games — RECALIBRATES and overwrites bands.json

suites.title: Content pack schema
suites.proves: Every bundled content pack validates against its Zod schema, and malformed packs are rejected loudly rather than half-loaded.
suites.doesNotProve: That a pack AGREES with the engine reading it. The rulesVersion check is deliberately deferred to whoever builds the downloadable-pack loader — bundled packs ship in the same commit as their engine, so such a check would compare a constant against a constant. PHASE1_BRIEF §6 seam 7.

crossCutting.explanation: Not a suite, and should not become one. Every suite above carries its own negative controls, because a control belongs next to the check it falsifies — moving them into a shared 'negative suite' would separate each control from the thing it exists to break. The manifest counts them per suite instead, and manifest.test.ts rejects any suite declaring zero.

Two mechanisms, neither subsuming the other, and the second is why this is not simply a dependency-cruiser run. dependency-cruiser enforces the import-graph half; exports.test.ts enforces the half a graph CANNOT see, asserting every data export of the engine is the SAME OBJECT as content's, by identity — because a table re-declared inside packages/engine imports nothing and so casts no edge on the graph.

Three invariants inside the property suite, not a suite of its own: viewstate-round-trip, gamestate-round-trip and undo-round-trip. All three are invisible to the equivalence corpus BY CONSTRUCTION — rig.ts normalise() round-trips both engines through JSON before hashing, so anything JSON destroys is destroyed identically on both sides and the hashes still match. gamestate-round-trip was added at P2.1 and is NOT redundant with the viewState one: viewState is a projection that drops 13 of GameState's 53 keys including the deck, so a defect in any of those 13 is invisible to it. Its control asserts exactly that asymmetry — one saboteur, gamestate-round-trip fires, viewstate-round-trip does not. Phase 2 Storage serialises GameState, so this is the property that save-and-resume is built on. PHASE1_BRIEF §7 asked for a whole serialisation SUITE and it was never built; this is the half Phase 2 depends on.

There is no suite testing each engine rule in isolation, and this file will not pretend otherwise. §7 describes one; the disk does not have one. What exists is the equivalence corpus, which proves agreement with legacy, and the property suite, which proves ten stated invariants. Neither is a unit suite and neither claims to be. Note the converse too: the corpus realises NO §7 row — the largest test asset in this repository, 315 assertions and 2,000 nightly games, does not appear in that table at all, which is the other half of why the table could not simply be transcribed. Whether a unit suite is worth building is a real question for a later phase. Recording that it is absent is not a criticism of the repository — it is the precondition for anyone reasoning correctly about what is proven here.
